description: This Federation of American Scientists report asks what electro-optical satellite imagery can show about hyperscale AI data centre development and what policymakers can learn from it, and it fills a gap by giving a baseline assessment of the benefits and limitations. Two case studies are presented: tracking construction at Khazna's Ajman data centre in the United Arab Emirates, and feature identification at xAI's Colossus site in Memphis, Tennessee. They reveal inconsistencies between commercial announcements and activity visible in imagery. The report has a methodology, opportunities and challenges of imagery for monitoring, key takeaways, recommendations and an appendix. Producer: the report was written for and funded by the 2025 GovAI Fall Fellowship, edited by FAS, and draws on Epoch AI's Frontier Data Centers Hub. Coverage: two facilities. Access: free web page. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: two sites only and imagery dates were not listed on the page section read. Simulation uses: it documents how construction and capacity can be observed independently, useful for capacity-planning and monitoring models of data centres. Related records: none linked.
